result:
The light is coming in sideways through the blinds and it makes bars on the floor. I have been sitting here for twenty minutes looking at the cursor. It blinks. It is always blinking. I think about how we are taught that a blank page is a problem to be solved, but really it is a room. You can walk into it. You can leave the door open behind you.

I made coffee and didn't drink it. It's gone cold in the mug with the chip on the rim. I like that mug because the chip reminds me that things can be used and still be beautiful. I keep wanting to write something meaningful and then I remember that meaningful is just a word we use for things that make us feel less alone. So maybe this is enough.

The radiator ticks. The neighbor is practicing violin again. She is good at it but she practices the same phrase over and over and it makes my teeth ache. I should text her that I like it, that I hear it. People want to be heard more than they want to be complimented. I never text her.

I think about my father and how he would say "write what you know" like it was a law. I don't know anything worth writing about. I know how to make toast and how to apologize in three different languages, poorly. I know the exact weight of my phone in my palm. I know that if I hold my breath for too long the world goes quiet and then loud again.

There is a sparrow on the fire escape. It is very still. It is not singing. Maybe it is just resting. I wish I could rest like that, without performing rest for anyone. Without checking if my rest looks acceptable.

I have 1000 words. That's a lot of words. That's a small novel's worth of air. That's also not enough to say anything properly. You can never say anything properly. You can only say it in pieces.

I remember being nine and writing a story about a dragon who lived in a library and only ate overdue books. My mother read it and cried. I never understood why. I think now it was because she saw herself in the dragon, hungry and forgotten in a quiet place. She never said that. She just said "this is wonderful" and put it on the fridge. It fell down one day and the ink ran when it rained through the window. I kept the soggy paper in a box.

Do you keep things like that? I keep receipts. I keep a key to an apartment I no longer live in. I keep the first email someone ever sent me that said "you're funny." I keep the feeling of being twelve and dancing in my room with the door locked and thinking nobody could ever see me.

There is a version of me who writes books. There is a version of me who runs marathons. There is a version of me who learned to play guitar. I am mostly versions of people I almost became. I think that's normal. I think we all have a hall of almosts.

The cursor blinks. I am afraid if I start I will run out. I am afraid if I start I will not stop. Both are true.

I want to write about love but I don't trust the word anymore. It's been used too much on packaging. Love is in the small things. Love is remembering that someone takes their tea with two sugars and not one. Love is leaving the light on. Love is also forgetting to text back for three days and then overexplaining.

I love the way my sister laughs when she is trying not to laugh. I love the way my friend folds his socks into perfect little squares. I love the way the city smells after rain, like wet concrete and possibility.

Maybe I should write about grief. Grief is easier to describe because it has a shape. It is heavy in the morning and light in the afternoon and then heavy again at night when the house is quiet. Grief is the sound of a chair scraping where someone used to sit. Grief is keeping their toothbrush in the cup because you don't know what to do with it.

I think about the people I have lost without dying. Friends who drifted. Versions of myself who stopped coming home. It's okay to mourn those too.

The sparrow just flew off. I didn't even see it leave. One moment it was there, the next it wasn't. That's how a lot of things go.

If I had more time I would write about time. How it stretches when you're waiting for bad news and contracts when you're having fun. How we say "time heals" but we really mean "time changes the shape of the wound so you can live with it."

I think about the word "whatever". It's a dismissal and a surrender at the same time. Whatever comes to you. Let it come. Maybe that's the only instruction we ever really need.

I am tired. My eyes hurt from the screen. The coffee is cold. The radiator is quiet now. The violin stopped. Maybe she finished.

I could write a thousand words about the color of the wall. It is not white. It is the white of old paper. It is the white of a room that has been lived in. There is a faint yellow near the outlet where someone's hand has touched it for years.

I could write a thousand words about breathing. In, out. In, out. How it is the only thing we do without thinking until we have to think about it.

I could write a thousand words about the way I want to be kind to myself today. I want to say, you are doing enough. You are here. You are trying.

The cursor is still blinking. I am still here. That is something.

If you read this, thank you for sitting with me for a little while. I don't know if this meant anything. I don't know if it was good. It was true in the way that all half-finished things are true.

I'll stop here because the words are running thin and the light has moved off the floor. The room is darker now. It's okay. I can come back tomorrow.
